core.title: Name every wagon URN wagon:{kebab-case-name}, built via the stack's wagon-URN builder
core.given: A wagon URN is being assigned or constructed — in a plan artifact, manifest, spec, implementation code or generation code, by any author.
core.when: You create, rename or build the wagon's URN.
core.then: Build the wagon URN through the stack's designated wagon-URN construction construct (profile key urn.builder.wagon) so it is wagon:{kebab-case-name}, matching the wagon URN shape (profile key urn.wagon).
prefer: A verb-object slug that names what the wagon does (e.g. resolve-dilemmas, commit-state).
Valid forms as in the source: wagon:resolve-dilemmas, wagon:burn-timebank, wagon:manage-users.
avoid: Hand-assembling the wagon URN string instead of using the stack's designated wagon-URN builder (urn.builder.wagon).
Uppercase, underscores, spaces, dots or a leading digit/hyphen in the name part.
Noun-only or vague slugs when a verb-object slug fits.
core.why: Feature URNs, trains and slug/dirname conversion all derive from the wagon URN, so a single predictable kebab grammar built through one construction path keeps references and generated paths consistent.
evidence: Every declared wagon URN matches the wagon URN shape (urn.wagon).
Wagon URNs constructed in code or generated artifacts are produced via the stack's designated wagon-URN builder (urn.builder.wagon), not hand-assembled strings.
verification: Hard check: every declared wagon URN is matched against the profile's wagon URN shape (urn.wagon); a mismatch is a finding. The verb-object slug form is a preference, not a hard failure.

Construction check: a wagon URN constructed in code or in a generated artifact must come from the stack's wagon-URN builder (urn.builder.wagon); a hand-built wagon URN string literal at a construction site is a finding.
The check accepts the known-valid examples wagon:resolve-dilemmas, wagon:burn-timebank, wagon:manage-users.

Detecting the change-based activation requires a diff-level observer that extracts added/changed wagon URN values and new wagon-URN construction sites (string literals vs designated-builder calls); mere references to an existing, unchanged wagon URN are not findings.

values: any file declaring a wagon URN
wagon URN constructed/assigned in code or generator

fires: A new wagon manifest is authored and its URN assigned
An existing wagon is renamed and its URN changes
A plan artifact or spec declares a new wagon URN
Implementation or generation code assigns or constructs a new wagon URN
doesNotFire: Editing a wagon's plan artifacts (e.g. WMBTs) or acceptances without touching its URN
Naming a feature, train or artifact URN (governed by their own naming conventions)
Code or docs that only reference an existing, unchanged wagon URN

profileRequirements.meaning: The exact wagon URN shape (grammar) that every declared or constructed wagon URN must match; the core's then/evidence/verification refer to it generically.
The stack's designated construct by which code builds a wagon URN; wagon URNs constructed in code or generated artifacts must be produced through it, never hand-assembled strings.

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's designated construct (e.g. a builder method) by which code constructs a wagon URN; wagon URNs constructed in code or generated artifacts must be produced through it rather than hand-assembled strings.
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The urn group carries only shapes (urn.<artifact>), binding syntax (urn.binding.<artifact>) and plan-artifact declaration (urn.declaration); no key names the code construct that constructs a URN, and tooling.urn_resolver covers only resolution. Proposed as the concrete wagon instance; generalizing to a parametric urn.builder.<artifact> family (acceptance, feature, train, ...) is up to the vocabulary owner.

bunOnly.reason: Term/detector ids of this one rule are ATDD-Bun checker vocabulary; the core describes the grammar check generically and takes the pattern from urn.wagon.
Same realization term id; the preference-not-hard-failure scoping itself is stack-neutral and lives in core:verification.
The builder's concrete API name is a stack construct; the core activation refers to the profile key urn.builder.wagon instead.

classification.note: Scope over plan artifacts, manifests, specs, implementation and generation code kept; actor-neutral as in the source; no stack named.

Verb-object slug preference; the slug examples are URN-level, not stack-level.
Valid URN forms preserved verbatim; they instantiate the ATDD wagon URN scheme, not a stack.
Neutralized to 'the stack's designated wagon-URN builder'; the concrete URNBuilder.wagon is supplied by the profile key.
Character-level negations of the wagon URN grammar; the exact shape is carried by urn.wagon. Names no stack.
Prefix rule of the wagon URN scheme; stack-neutral.

The concrete pattern ^wagon:[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$ is spelled by the profile key urn.wagon.
Builder named via the profile key; obligation strength unchanged.
'Pattern is the hard check' -> core:verification; the pattern value -> urn.wagon; the term id wagon_urn_pattern is realization-only.

neutralityNotes: 'wagon' and the wagon:{kebab-case-name} scheme are treated as stack-neutral ATDD artifact concepts (the profile vocabulary itself parameterizes urn.<artifact> and layout.wagon_dir over wagon), so the core names the wagon URN directly while the exact pattern is carried by urn.wagon. The Bun 'built via URNBuilder.wagon' obligation is generalized to 'built via the stack's designated wagon-URN construction construct' through the proposed key urn.builder.wagon; with the Bun profile value URNBuilder.wagon the obligation is identical. The rule's term id (wagon_urn_pattern) and the builder's concrete API name remain realization details (bunOnly).
